3.tense: You are still at a door that has swung shut, one hand out for a feeling that hasn't come.
3.verb: opening to what might come before naming what it is
3.place: in the half-lit rooms where the next step is chosen
3.ask: Stop imagining what you began and make the next real move with it now — let it carry the size it takes.
3.core:
In the half-lit rooms lately, not much gets taken in. What could draw you passes by unclaimed. You can name what things are; letting them be more than that isn't happening right now. That's not a flaw in you. The room at the end is empty and standing where you are is easier than walking in.
Stop planning what you began and make the next real move with it now. Not imagining it. Making it. The size is whatever it is. The point is the door on this side, where you hand what you have forward. Small and actual beats possible and untouched. Once it has some size, you'll see whether you wanted it — and if you didn't, drop it. The handing was the point.
3.sheetLine: You can let something you started actually get bigger.

4.tense: You are steering without a hand on the wheel, in a room you keep saying you didn't pick.
4.verb: opening to what might come before naming what it is
4.place: in the half-lit rooms where the next step is chosen
4.ask: When someone gives you something for what you gave, receive it and say a plain thank-you.
4.core:
Your openings are yours. You've been filing them under circumstance, under the room, under someone else's draw. What you actually do is notice first, make it safe, and let something arrive at its own pace. That's a contribution, and you've been leaving it unsigned.
Let one exchange run both ways this week. Not a tally — one return. Someone hands you something for what you gave: a thanks, their time, a seat at the table, a favor. Receive it and don't wave it off, and when it lands, say thank you and mean it. Watch what comes back; that's how you see what you've been giving. If nothing comes back, note it. That's information, not a verdict on you.
4.sheetLine: The openings were yours. Let one come back.

1.tense: The heart is open right now, and nothing has been poured into it yet.
1.verb: opening to what hasn't arrived yet
1.place: where what you are comes out as what you do
1.ask: When a pull shows up this week, stay with it an hour and then stop. Leave it unsorted — no yes, no no.
1.core:
You can feel something before you know what it is, and that is where you are. A conversation, a project, a plan — one of them is tugging at you and you have not named it. The pull is the beginning, and you are letting it stay a pull, not rushing to close it into a decision.

That openness is also what you are made of. What you are becoming shows through most clearly when you let a thing interest you before you have decided what it is for. So follow a pull a little way, and hold there. The interest does not have to turn into a plan, and letting it stay open is not the same as avoiding the choice.
1.sheetLine: The pull is the beginning, and you are not rushing it.

2.tense: You will have the whole thing settled before it has a chance to arrive.
2.verb: opening to what hasn't arrived yet
2.place: where what you are comes out as what you do
2.ask: Choose something you have been leaving half-done and give it a real ending. Call it finished and act on that, once.
2.core:
An opening is barely here and you are already bracing for what happens after it. The feeling has not shown up and you have decided how it should land, what it should become, who it is for. You are completing who you are supposed to be before the feeling has shown you anything. Readiness gets spent on the shape of things rather than on the things themselves.

What settles it is finishing something cleanly. Not a fresh direction — one thing already in motion, given a real end. When a thing is finished on purpose, the bracing loses its job, and there is room again for what has not yet arrived.
2.sheetLine: You have decided the ending before the feeling lands.

3.tense: The moment to open has already passed, and you are standing there still.
3.verb: opening to what hasn't arrived yet
3.place: where what you are comes out as what you do
3.ask: Bring one of the ideas you keep turning over into something you can point to — make it once, at whatever size it comes out.
3.core:
You are set up to feel what is coming — that part of you is intact. But something that mattered got put down before it could finish, and since then you have been watching from behind the door. The readiness is there, and it has nowhere to land. Pulling back has been a way of not adding anything more to the pile, and it has started to look like who you are.

There is a way back that does not ask you to feel more. Make what has only ever existed as a thought into something once, at whatever size it comes out. You do not have to arrive anywhere. A single finished small act is enough for the door to swing open from the other side.
3.sheetLine: The readiness is there and it has nowhere to land.

1.tense: Something is beginning in you that you can feel and cannot yet name.
1.verb: opening to what can be felt before you know what it is
1.place: standing in the whole of it without stepping outside
1.ask: Follow a pull a single step before you decide what it is.
1.core:
Nothing has to be worked out yet. The pattern comes to you whole where you stand, and a feeling that is still only an edge can stay an edge for a while. You can let it be there without forcing a name onto it, and that is what is happening now.

So let a pull have you before you decide what it is. A person you keep thinking about, a room you keep passing, a song that comes back. Go one step toward it and see what is there. If nothing pulls, wait with an open hand and don't reach for a conclusion. The pull doesn't have to lead anywhere to be worth following.
1.sheetLine: You can feel a beginning before it has a name.

2.tense: You are already at the finish, braced for an ending that hasn't been written.
2.verb: opening to what can be felt before you know what it is
2.place: standing in the whole of it without stepping outside
2.ask: Take one piece of work to where it stands without you, then stop.
2.core:
In your version the pattern is already over. You are ahead of what is taking place, mapping the close before anything has had a middle. What is opening to you doesn't get to open at its own speed while the outcome is decided in your head.

Bring one thing to where it stands without your hands on it, then put your hands down. Not the biggest thing. Something with a shape that can be finished. Let it stand there. Then let the next one start without your direction. This is not asking you to be less able. It is asking you to let a thing arrive after you have left the room.
2.sheetLine: You're skipping the middle to get to the end.

3.tense: You are at a door that closed behind you and still waiting for it to open.
3.verb: opening to what can be felt before you know what it is
3.place: standing in the whole of it without stepping outside
3.ask: Bring what you began to the size it wants to be.
3.core:
The pattern still comes to you, but the paying attention has gone quiet. What you felt starting a while back, you set down. The open readiness is still here; it just has nothing in its hands. You are waiting to feel ready again instead of being ready here.

Carry what you already began to the size it wants to be. Not everything. A piece that still lives somewhere in you, the one you keep almost bringing up. Make one move that takes it forward. No feeling has to come first. Readiness is not something you wait for; it comes back when you start.
3.sheetLine: Something opened a while back and you set it down.

4.tense: You keep both sides of an exchange level without noticing that your hand is the one holding them.
4.verb: opening to what can be felt before you know what it is
4.place: standing in the whole of it without stepping outside
4.ask: Accept something small someone offers without hurrying to give back.
4.core:
The pattern comes to you whole, and that pattern takes in what the ones beside you are carrying. You have been the one squaring the exchange, watching what is owed and what is given, keeping the two sides level. Your version is that this is just how things are. Your hand is on the scale though.

Let one thing come to you this week without returning it right away. Accept something small that is offered, and leave the exchange alone for a day. If you do give, give what feels true rather than what matches. The fairness that flows without your prompting is the kind that doesn't need your eyes on both sides of the scale.
4.sheetLine: Your hand keeps the exchange level. That's just how things are.

1.tense: You are standing inside an openness that has not yet been asked to hold anything.
1.verb: Feeling something new and letting it arrive whole
1.place: Inside the moment where what you've made is complete and you hand it over
1.ask: When something pulls at you this week — a person, a place, an idea — follow it a little way before deciding whether it's yours. No commitment. Just let the pull happen first.
1.core:
Something has finished. You can feel it — the work, the stretch of time, the thing you were making, it has its shape now and it's not asking for more from you. And instead of bracing for the next thing, you're staying open. You're letting what comes next have its pull on you before you name it, and that's the right order. The openness isn't idle; it's how the next real thing finds you.

Keep it that way a little longer. Before you choose anything — whether to pick up the next project, whether to answer a message, whether to say yes — let the feeling of being drawn happen first, before you weigh it. You don't have to act. Just let it register. The choice gets clearer when the pull gets to speak first.
1.sheetLine: You can feel what's coming before you name it.

2.tense: You will keep reaching for the next shape before this one has settled into its form.
2.verb: Feeling something new and letting it arrive whole
2.place: Inside the moment where what you've made is complete and you hand it over
2.ask: Take what you've been steering and stop touching it for a week. Let it stand finished, without your hand on it, and see what holding that stillness costs.
2.core:
You're already at the next thing. Maybe the next three. The heart opened, the feeling arrived, and then — before it could land — you started shaping it. Finishing it. Making it hold. There's a future in your hands that hasn't happened yet, and you're already writing its ending, which means nothing you make can stay open long enough to feel alive. The completion you're forcing is real work, but it's your work, and it's standing where receiving should be.

Stop finishing for a moment. The next thing you're tempted to wrap up, leave it ajar. You will survive the unfinished edge. Let the moment be enough without you putting a lid on it.
2.sheetLine: You're finished before you've started.

3.tense: A door closed behind you and you are still waiting at it for it to open again.
3.verb: Feeling something new and letting it arrive whole
3.place: Inside the moment where what you've made is complete and you hand it over
3.ask: Find something you began that didn't get finished and carry it one step further than it went before. Not to complete it — just to let it be bigger than it stopped at.
3.core:
Something began in you and it did not get finished. The feeling came, the recognition was there, and then it stayed there. You're still waiting before it, expecting it to start, when it already did — back when you weren't looking. The ability to feel what's next is in you, but it's parked. You're at the threshold and you've been at the threshold so long the threshold has gone quiet. That is what this looks like on empty: the origin stopped, and you stopped with it.

Let it be bigger than it was. Not done — just further on than it stopped. The step doesn't have to be large.
3.sheetLine: The beginning already happened. You're still at the door.

4.tense: The one who kept things fair in the exchange has been there the whole time, and the voice you use for it is luck.
4.verb: Feeling something new and letting it arrive whole
4.place: Inside the moment where what you've made is complete and you hand it over
4.ask: Next time you give something — a hand, an answer, a piece of yourself — name what comes back to you. Say it quietly in your head: this is what is being received. Let the exchange be visible while it happens.
4.core:
You are the one who keeps things level. You hand things across the table and you take what comes back, and you do it without counting, which is exactly why it goes unseen. The fairness is real. The person doing it is you. Asked about it, you'd say you just happen to be around when it's needed. The making of it is the part you aren't signing.

Watch the next exchange with someone as it happens. See yourself giving. See yourself receiving, even the small returns — a thank you, a hand with something heavy, a moment of attention. Nothing has to change. Just let the exchange be visible to you while it's happening. The hand you are not seeing is yours.
4.sheetLine: The fairness in this exchange is your doing.
